chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibrahim ibn Abi Sammal from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Then you circle the House seven times, and while circling you say: 'O Allah, I ask You by Your Name by which one walks upon the surface of the water as one walks upon the firm ground of the earth; and I ask You by Your Name by which Your Throne trembles; and I ask You by Your Name by which the feet of Your angels tremble; and I ask You by Your Name by which Musa called You from the side of Mount Tur, and You answered him, and cast love for him from Yourself; and I ask You by Your Name by which You forgave - for Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) - what preceded of his sin and what followed, and You completed Your favor upon him, that You do for me such and such, whatever You love of supplication.'
Abu Ishaq said (1): Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar narrated this supplication from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

And whenever you reach the door of the Ka'bah, pray upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and say while circling: 'O Allah, I am poor to You, and I am fearful seeking refuge, so do not change my name nor alter my body.'

When you reach the rear of the Ka'bah, which is the 'place of refuge' slightly before the Yemeni Corner, in the seventh lap, spread your hands on the ground and press your cheek and belly to the House, then say: 'O Allah, the House is Your House, and the servant is Your servant, and this is the place of the one seeking refuge in You from the Fire.'
Then acknowledge to your Lord the sins you have committed, for there is no believing servant who acknowledges his sins to his Lord in this place but that Allah will forgive him, if He wills.
For Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to his servants, 'Clear the way for me so that I may acknowledge to my Lord what I have done.'

O Allah, from You comes relief, deliverance, and health. O Allah, my deed is weak, so multiply it for me, and forgive me what You have observed of me which was hidden from Your creation; and you seek refuge in Allah from the Fire, and choose for yourself from the supplications.

Then face the Yemeni Corner and the Corner containing the Black Stone, and conclude with it; and if you cannot, it will not harm you, and you say: 'O Allah, suffice me with what You have provided me and bless me in what You have given me.'

Then you come to the Station of Ibrahim and pray two rak'ahs, making it in front of you, and recite in them the Surah of Unity [«Say: He is Allah, the One»] and in the second rak'ah: «Say: O you disbelievers».
Then you recite the Tashahhud, praise Allah, extol Him, pray upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and ask Him to accept from you.
These two rak'ahs are the obligatory prayer; it is not disliked for you to pray them at any time you wish, at sunrise and at sunset.
Then you come to the Black Stone, kiss it and touch it, or gesture towards it, for it is necessary to do so.
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and rituals during the circumambulation of the Ka'bah according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the comprehensive ritual of Tawaf, emphasizing the spiritual intimacy of reciting specific supplications while circumambulating the Ka'bah. It highlights the Station of Ibrahim as the site for the two rak'ahs of prayer, linking the physical act of worship to the legacy of Prophet Ibrahim, and concludes with the essential act of kissing or gesturing to the Black Stone as a culmination of the ritual.
